assessment.summary: TREM2 is a well-validated immunoreceptor target with excellent structural data (15 PDB entries, best at 1.47Å, 11 ligand-bound) confirming a druggable extracellular binding pocket. Despite absent ChEMBL IC50 entries, a first-in-human oral small-molecule agonist (VG-3927/SAR448851) was reported in 2026, confirming small-molecule tractability. Strong disease validation in Alzheimer's disease and other conditions, combined with 841+ publications, supports high overall druggability.
evidence_gaps: ChEMBL has zero IC50 entries — likely a data lag given known small-molecule programs, but quantitative SAR data is not publicly available
No approved drugs exist; clinical programs are at first-in-human stage
Context-dependent agonist vs. antagonist biology complicates therapeutic strategy (neurodegeneration vs. cancer)
CNS penetration and blood-brain barrier permeability data for small-molecule agonists not yet publicly disclosed
Intracellular signaling domain (DAP12 interaction interface) is structurally less characterized
Selectivity data against other TREM family members (TREM1) is not captured in available databases
